budget_items.topic: Abatement and motor vehicle excise abatement requests for May
budget_items.what_was_said: The office processed a batch of abatement requests and a large number of motor vehicle excise tax abatements for the month, tied to late payment processing by the tax collector.

budget_items.topic: FY2027 preliminary real estate and personal property tax bills/warrant
budget_items.what_was_said: The board reviewed and prepared to sign preliminary FY2027 real estate and personal property tax billing warrants and commitments; personal property bills were clarified as business/professional taxes, not household property.

budget_items.topic: FY2026 supplemental real estate tax bills
budget_items.what_was_said: The board noted these supplemental bills were already signed/approved the prior month, with no new supplemental bills added this cycle.

Residents can defer property taxes, with the deferred amount accumulating against the property at a stated interest rate; the town currently has no active deferral applicants after one incomplete late application last year.

budget_items.topic: Chapter land lien release recording fee
budget_items.what_was_said: Releasing a chapter-land tax lien when a property leaves agricultural (61A) classification requires paying back taxes and a fee to record the release at the Registry of Deeds.

budget_items.topic: Vision vendor quote to update property record cards
budget_items.what_was_said: The board discussed paying an outside vendor to update yearly property record cards after in-house software/PC issues made the process cumbersome, calling the cost well worth it.

The consultant's report proposed applying a combined waterfront valuation factor derived from recent lake-area sales, split into a base factor plus a per-lake sub-neighborhood adjustment, replacing outdated 'good/average/below average' waterfront ratings.
The board discussed Clause 18, a discretionary one-time tax relief tool for taxpayers in dire financial straits, noting the town has no applicants and has not yet finalized criteria for granting it.

budget_items.topic: Senior means-tested tax exemption / circuit breaker
budget_items.what_was_said: The board discussed Lunenburg's locally adopted senior means-tested exemption, which requires filing a federal tax return and qualifying for the state circuit breaker credit, described as a substantial tax break for eligible seniors.

decisions.decision: Board endorsed dedicating a separate server at town hall for GIS map updates so the principal assessor's laptop is no longer tied up for days during updates.
Board agreed to restore both property record card views on the website, with the more frequently updated one clearly labeled 'in process' to avoid confusing residents.
Board agreed to eliminate the 'average' and 'below average' waterfront quality ratings entirely and instead apply valuation factors based on actual property quality.
Board indicated the town intends to acquire the chapter-land property at issue, pending a letter from the Select Board.
Board set July 1, August 5, and September 2 as tentative dates for its next meetings, planning to meet only monthly over the summer.

minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors reorganized with a new member, elected officers, and paid tribute to the outgoing principal assessor for stabilizing the office, fixing chapter-land liens, and recovering missed new growth. Most of the meeting covered signing FY2027 preliminary tax warrants and commitments, ongoing GIS/mapping vendor troubles, and a consultant's report on overhauling the town's inconsistent waterfront property valuation neighborhoods, which the board agreed to continue revising. No members of the public were present or commented, and the board set its next three meeting dates before adjourning.

what_happened.line: The board agreed to drop the "average" and "below average" waterfront quality ratings and apply valuation factors based on actual property quality instead, following a consultant's report on inconsistent waterfront neighborhoods.
The board signed and authorized the FY2027 preliminary real estate and personal property tax warrants and commitments.
The board reorganized, electing a new chair, vice chair and clerk.
The board indicated the town intends to acquire the chapter-land property at issue, pending a letter from the Select Board.
No members of the public attended or commented.

why_it_matters: A change to how waterfront neighborhoods are valued can shift individual tax bills for lakefront property owners once the new factors are applied.
Signing the FY2027 preliminary tax warrants keeps the town's tax billing cycle on schedule for residents and businesses.
A town acquisition of the chapter-land parcel, if it goes forward, would resolve an outstanding agricultural-classification tax dispute on that property.
